remedy: MM1: PASS today means only that the MEMS lane is CARRYING rather than STATIC -- there is no level window in the check. A FAIL needs AN_EN up and the lane still static, which is the PDM clock or the mic; with AN_EN down the lane is static by definition and the runner says NO DATA. Check the panel ribbon first -- it is the same one ML-P1/ML-P2 use.
explain: MM1: the idle half of the one SP1/MM1 capture (S102) — the MEMS lane at the DSP (dsp4_rxscan.py on the MEMS input): lane not stuck, idle noise floor in range
pass_when: MM1: lane alive; floor within the declared window

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The run needs the matrix bus to itself, so the mixer is stopped for it; this display stays up throughout.
remedy: SP1: PASS wants the 1 kHz tone on the MEMS lane at least 20 dB above its idle floor, and the floor back within 3 dB when the tone stops. The runner asserts the route and READS IT BACK before it measures anything, so a FAIL here is the analog half and not the DSP: codec AOUT1L (analog U3 pin 22) -> C23 -> SPKR -> J59.12 = J42.12 -> the TS482 (digital U32) -> SPKR0/SPKR1 -> lswitch J1.6/7 -> the speaker in J2. Check the J2 speaker lead and the J13 = lswitch J1 panel FPC before suspecting the codec. A dark MEMS lane in BOTH legs is MM1's fault and not this row's -- read row 56 first.
explain: SP1: the tone half of the same capture — assert the route (below), inject TEST_OSC at 1 kHz into strip 20, read the MEMS lane, then tone off and read again
pass_when: SP1: the 1 kHz tone appears on the MEMS lane ≥ 20 dB above its idle floor; tone off → floor returns within 3 dB

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The run needs the matrix bus to itself, so the mixer is stopped for it; this display stays up throughout.
remedy: DC1: One chip select is asserted at a time, and ONLY CS1 AND CS2 CAN REACH A VERDICT -- CS5/CS6 have no part behind them and CS7/CS8 are not DSP selects at all (they are the CM4's SWD_EN1/EN3), so those four read NO DATA and that is not a fault. CS3/CS4 are no longer here: they are SPI_RDY and DY1 tests them. A FAIL on CS1 or CS2 is that select's routing or the part behind it; if BOTH fail it is the shared path, so confirm the DSPs are booted (DR2) first.\nDC2: The identity check is that the part behind the select reports CHIP_ID equal to the select number -- fw.csv declares a pin and a net, not a part number, so there is nothing else on the wire to match against. A mismatch is the wrong image staged far more often than the wrong part. As DC1, only CS1 and CS2 can reach a verdict.
explain: DC1: the CM4 asserts one select at a time and clocks a read of a known register on the part behind it; the others stay high. *H1S1 does not and must not assert any of them — all eight of its CS pins are GPIO_Input by decision (D8 amendment; ~/build-h1s1 Core/Src/main.c MX_GPIO_Init_2), and the CM4 masters the boot bus directly*\nDC2: the selected part's identity (SHARC: a DSP heartbeat/build-id cell; CPLD: design-id per dsp4_logic_id.py) matches the fw.csv Dsp*n* row
pass_when: DC1: the addressed part answers with the expected value; a read with all selects high returns nothing. Only CS1 and CS2 can reach a verdict (S100): CS6 reaches no fitted part *and* no read path, CS7/CS8 are not DSP selects at all — they carry the CM4's SWD_EN1/EN3. CS5 has no row here at all — old row 107. CS5 → renamed MicGainLatch in fw.csv (PW ruling, 2026-09-24): it is the CM4's drive for the mic-gain chain latch !CS_M, not a DSP chip-select. Tested as part of MC1/MC2/MC3 below, not as its own row — see those\nDC2: CHIP_ID equals the select number — the right part is populated behind the right select. GATING (S99): a wiring check wearing an id. BUILD_ID and the S82-signed build triple are evidence

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The run needs the matrix bus to itself, so the mixer is stopped for it; this display stays up throughout.
remedy: DY1: CS3 and CS4 are not chip selects: they carry DSPA's and DSPB's SPI2_RDY flow control back to the CM4, and DY1 checks the line FOLLOWS the part -- LOW while !RST_D is held low, HIGH once the part is at BOOT_STAGE 7, both read with the CM4's pull-down forced on so the card's 10K pulldown cannot be mistaken for a drive. Stuck LOW is an open net, an unbonded PB_05, or a part that never ran; stuck HIGH is a short to 3V3 on that net. If the part did not come back at all the row says NO DATA and DR2 is the row to read.
explain: DY1: CS3/CS4 are not chip selects: they carry DSPA's and DSPB's SPI2_RDY flow-control output back to the CM4 (GPIO8 / GPIO12; hardware-map.md §3, dsp4_boot.py RDY_GPIO). Read the line with the CM4's own pull-down forced on — each part carries a 10K pulldown to GND (R34/R22), so a HIGH can only be the part driving the pin — at three points of the run's own reset+boot recipe: with the pair up, with !RST_D held low, and after boot_pair() brings it back
pass_when: DY1: the line follows the part: LOW while !RST_D is held low (pad high-Z, the pulldowns win) and HIGH once that chip reads BOOT_STAGE >= 7 (SPI2 flow control driving, FCEN=1 FCPL=1). Both halves are required; a static level proves neither. A chip that does not come back at all is NO DATA here — that is DR2's verdict to give
manual: DY1: the three levels and BOOT_STAGE, per chip

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The app stays up and the colour changes when it finishes.
remedy:
NW1: PASS wants link up, 1000Mb/s, Full duplex. No link at all is the cable or J7; a link that comes up at 100Mb/s is the cable or the magnetics, not the CM4. Swap the cable to a known-good one before suspecting the board.
NW2: rx/tx errors, dropped and overruns must all be zero across the run, against a 30 s idle control. Non-zero counters on a link that is otherwise up point at the cable or the switch port -- swap the cable and re-run.
NW3: NW3 pings the bench host AND, as a control, the unit's own default gateway one switch hop away -- three 200-packet passes each, scored on the WORST. Loss to the bench host alone with the gateway clean is NO DATA, not FAIL: the runner will not blame the unit for someone else's path. A FAIL means loss appeared toward BOTH targets, which is the unit's own link -- swap the RJ45 cable and the switch port, then re-run.
NW4: NW4 runs iperf3 with the SERVER ON THE UNIT and the driving host as client, both directions, and wants at least 900 Mbit/s each way. If the driving host's own link is slower than gigabit the number measures that link and the runner says NO DATA rather than inventing a defect. A real FAIL is a gigabit path that will not carry gigabit: cable, switch port, or the PHY.
explain: HD0-1: cat /sys/class/drm/card*-HDMI-A-1/status; edid-decode < /sys/class/drm/card*-HDMI-A-1/edid (or xxd); cat …/modes; kmsprint or modetest -c for the active CRTC mode\nHD0-2: record …/status and the DRM hotplug/uevent count at start; re-read every 60 s for the soak window (≥ 1 h; 24 h for a shipping proof)
pass_when: HD0-1: status connected; EDID parses with a manufacturer + product code; the native mode is in modes and is the active mode\nHD0-2: status never leaves connected; hotplug count unchanged

spec_section: C. Read from the DSPs

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The run needs the matrix bus to itself, so the mixer is stopped for it; this display stays up throughout.
remedy: ML1: Reads a known H1S1 cell three times over /dev/ttyAMA0 -> MH1 -> H1S1. A FAIL here is the bus, not the cell. Check H1S1 is running (row 203), that the M MCU is passing traffic (row 202), and that no other tool on the CM4 is holding the UART.
explain: ML-M: the dispatcher answers the ? loopback probe only before S_RUN — so: read a cell through it (any ML1 read proves the path) and read MH1's own version if it publishes one
pass_when: ML-M: ML1 PASS — that is the whole verdict. The version read is evidence only (S99)
manual: ML-M: as ML1
spec_section: B. Read through H1S1 over the matrix bus

short: No action needed — press START TEST. The app stays up and the colour changes when it finishes.
remedy: HD0-1: PASS wants status=connected, an EDID that parses, and the native mode actually active. Reseat the HDMI FPC at both ends (J28 on the Digital board, and the TFT end). If the EDID parses but the mode is wrong the link is fine and the mode was overridden -- check config.txt and hdmi-full-rgb.service before touching the cable.\nHD0-2: The soak FAILs only if the status actually LEFT 'connected' during the window -- a marginal FPC seating, or the TFT rail dipping: reseat the FPC and check link 'hdmi-pwr' (row 152). A window shorter than the spec's hour is NO DATA, not FAIL, and the hotplug count is recorded as evidence but does not decide the verdict.
explain: ML1: read one H1S1 local cell (Sys001Test001 = 5414 is the known one) three times\nML2: read the H1S1 firmware-version cell
pass_when: ML1: three identical, well-formed answers within the bus timeout\nML2: non-zero, equals the version in /home/app/firmware/H1S1.shex's manifest. INFORMATIONAL (S99): does not gate the row — ML1 already proves the same part is present and answering
manual: ML1: the value, response time\nML2: version string both sides
